mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a recessionary demand shock, which reduces corporate earnings and increases risk aversion, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during such episodes, or the median return is not below the baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in INDPRO and a fall in HOUST over one month indicates supply-side inflation (strong output, constrained housing supply), which erodes real corporate earnings and increases inflation risk, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0% MoM AND HOUST < 0% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 0.5% combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 2.5% YoY signals a failed easing, increasing inflation uncertainty and risk premium, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in these episodes, or the mechanism fails to outperform a flat benchmark.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals rising household savings and reduced consumption, which forecasts lower corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes, or the median return is not below the historical median at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS above 0.5% MoM and a fall in UNRATE below 3.5% signals labor market softening, which reduces wage growth and supports corporate margins, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM AND UNRATE < 3.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered months, or the average return is not above the baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in HOUST above its 6-month moving average for at least 3 months signals rising housing demand and consumer confidence, which boosts retail and construction sector earnings, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails to outperform a naive momentum strategy at 5% significance.
